title: Annotatio IV §.V: First Christians’ koinonia with Apostles = communion with Father and Theanthropos Son — spiritual
pass_a_gloss: Of which first Christians, so to speak, there was by this pact Communion or koinōnia with the Apostles, and as of those, so of any rightly communicating through all ages with the same, and therewith at once koinōnia with the heavenly Father and with His Son the God-man Jesus Christ, always to remain (1 John 1:3); yet Spiritual, seeing that Christ, although He came not by water only but by water and blood.
pass_b_english: So the first Christians’ koinōnia with the Apostles — and of every rightly communicating person through all ages — is at once communion with the heavenly Father and with His Son the God-man Jesus Christ (1 John 1:3), always to remain.
Yet it is Spiritual: Christ came not by water only but by water and blood.
source_text: Quorum Christianorum puta primorum hoc pacto Communio seu koinōnia fuit, cum Apostolis fuit, & uti istorum, ita ritè communicantium quorumvis, per omnia secula, cum iisdem, eoque simul koinōnia meta tou patros kai meta tou huiou Iēsou Christou, Communio & cum Patre Cœlesti & cum Filio ejus Theanthrōpō Jesu Christo, semperq; mansura, 1. Joh. 1. 3.; at Spiritualis, quandoquidem Christus, utut venit non tō hydati monon, all' en tō hydati kai tō haimati.
notes: Koinonia with Father and Theanthropos; spiritual.
